senses.gloss:
A-mūlā (‘without root’) is the name in the Atharvaveda^1 of
a plant (Methonica superba), which was used for poisoning
arrows. Bloomfield,^2 however, renders it as ‘movable property.’
1) v. 314. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien,
18, 286; Whitney, Translation of the
Atharvaveda, 279, accepts ‘rootless
(plant).’
2) Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 457.
